props.title: Puppet Master
props.initialSlug: Killer dolls hunt victims in sinister hotel

sections.content: Puppet Master launched one of horror's most enduring direct-to-video franchises, blending killer doll mayhem with occult Nazi experiments. Charles Band's Full Moon Features struck gold with this tale of psychic researchers investigating animated puppets created by André Toulon. The film cleverly builds on earlier killer doll movies like Child's Play (1988) and Dolls (1987), but adds unique elements like each puppet having distinct powers and personalities. Blade, Pinhead, Leech Woman and others became iconic horror characters, spawning 13+ sequels.

sections.content: The franchise's mythology deepens with each entry, particularly in Puppet Master III: Toulon's Revenge (1991), which explores the puppets' origins in Nazi Germany. This prequel adds tragic depth to Toulon's character while maintaining the series' signature mix of practical effects and stop-motion animation. The practical puppet effects, though dated, showcase impressive craftsmanship that influenced later films like Dolls (1987) and Demonic Toys (1992).

Full Moon's success with Puppet Master inspired numerous imitators in the 90s killer toy subgenre. Films like Dollman vs. Demonic Toys (1993) and Blood Dolls (1999) tried capturing similar magic but lacked Puppet Master's distinctive characters and mythology. The franchise's influence extends to modern films like Annabelle (2014) and M3GAN (2022), proving the enduring appeal of killer doll horror. SUBHEAD: Legacy and Modern Impact

movies.title: Retro Puppet Master
movies.slug: Young Toulon learns puppet animation magic in 1902 Paris

sections.content: While later entries like Puppet Master: The Legacy (2003) relied heavily on recycled footage, the series found new life with Puppet Master: The Littlest Reich (2018). This reboot embraced ultra-violence and dark humor, starring Thomas Lennon and featuring effects by special effects legend Tom Savini. The original's influence on indie horror continues, seen in films like The Boy (2016) and Brahms: The Boy II (2020).
